description: Verify that DUT's ARP Reply carries its own iface IPv4 as sender_proto_ip — the field that lets the requester populate cache with the resolved <IP, MAC> binding (RFC 826 §2.4)
approach:
[Objective]
For the requester to successfully cache the resolution, sender_proto_ip on the Reply must be the very IP the request asked about — i.e. DUT's iface IP. Wrong values poison the requester's cache.

[Scenario — chronological]
1. Tester → DUT: ARP Request (target_ip=DUT IP)

2. Observation (3 s window):
   • DUT → Tester: ARP Reply
      - sender_proto_ip == DUT iface IPv4   ← key check
      - sender_mac      == DUT iface MAC
      - opcode          == 2

[Pass condition]
Reply's sender_proto_ip equals DUT iface IPv4.

[Fail condition]
• Fail_sender_ip_not_dut — Reply emitted but sender_proto_ip differed
• Fail_no_reply — DUT did not respond

verdicts.Pass: Reply sender_proto_ip matched DUT iface IPv4 — normal
verdicts.Fail_sender_ip_not_dut: Reply emitted but sender_proto_ip ≠ DUT iface IPv4
verdicts.Fail_no_reply: DUT did not respond to the Request
